source_updates.title: RESTORE: REal-time Steerable Music resTORation and bandwidth Extension via stem disentanglement
findings: HTDemucs is adapted to six additive stems: vocals, music, broadband hiss, transient noise, residual, and HFE
training degradations and the 30-item paired test are synthetic; distortion and groove echo are omitted
real historical recordings have no clean target and are assessed with reference-free distribution metrics
HFE is not uniformly favourable across reported CLAP-FAD categories and no listening study is reported
approximately 50-times-real-time throughput is measured on one A100 and does not establish CPU or low-latency deployment
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Mixture-consistent semantic stems and isolated HFE are promising controls; HFE must remain opt-in and requires identity, transient, stereo, mono, peak, and listener validation.

source_updates.title: Spot, Separate, and Enhance: Fully Generative Approach for Audio Mixing
findings: SSE is a multimodal generative UGC or movie-audio enhancement model, not a conventional multitrack music mixer
DegradedMix uses separator-derived pseudo-stems followed by synthetic gain, noise, and reverberation changes
text instructions are generated from the clean target and may provide privileged information unavailable in ordinary prompts
the roughly three-billion-parameter large model is trained on two RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs
main objective metrics do not protect waveform identity, transients, phase, loudness, or true peak
the 10-participant 10-video pairwise study does not document loudness matching, listener screening, or equivalence bounds
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Generative UGC enhancement candidate, not evidence for autonomous music mixing; require no-generation baselines, source-preservation measures, and loudness-matched listening before transfer.

findings: no commit license checkpoint environment or inference script can be pinned
no public code weights or split manifest verified

knowledge_cards: Exact additive reconstruction constrains the sum but does not prove semantic correctness of each stem.
Generated high-frequency extension should be isolated and opt-in.
Reference-free FAD on historical recordings is distribution evidence, not archival fidelity or preference.
RESTORE HFE is not uniformly favourable across its own reported CLAP-FAD categories.
Single-A100 throughput does not guarantee CPU, plug-in, memory, or low-latency performance.
An empty linked repository blocks reproducibility despite public demonstrations.
SSE concerns generative UGC or movie enhancement rather than multitrack music mixing.
Separator-produced pseudo-stems can transfer leakage and artefacts into targets and evaluation.
Clean-target-generated instructions can be oracle-like compared with real ambiguous prompts.
Embedding and distribution metrics do not protect waveform identity, attacks, phase, loudness, or true peak.
A small preference test without documented loudness matching or screening is limited task evidence.
Generative replacement and conservative enhancement need separate baselines and acceptance criteria.
